memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Before they had gone to bed, all the men from every part of the city of Sodom - both young and old - surrounded the house. They called to Lot, "Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us so that we can have sex with them." - Gen 19:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a dark and disturbing scene, and Scripture does not hide it. The entire city - "both young and old," "every part" - surrounds Lot's house, demanding to violently abuse his guests. This is not a private sin but a whole society given over to cruelty, predatory violence, and the wish to harm the vulnerable stranger. The sin of Sodom was total; the corruption reached everyone.

We should read this honestly. The horror of the scene is the point. The men of Sodom sought to commit violent assault against helpless guests - a monstrous violation of both hospitality and human dignity. This is what a culture becomes when it fully abandons God: the strong prey on the weak, and cruelty becomes normal, even celebrated, from the youngest to the oldest.

The Bible elsewhere names Sodom's sins broadly - pride, gluttony, indifference to the poor and needy, and unconcern for justice (Ezek 16:49) - alongside the violence and immorality we see here. A society rots from many directions at once when it turns from God.

This is a sobering warning, not for pointing fingers, but for humble self-examination. Any culture, any heart, that pushes God out will drift toward using and harming others. The only safeguard is a people who "act justly, love mercy, and walk humbly" with God (Mic 6:8). Against such darkness, God's people are called to be light - protecting the vulnerable rather than preying on them.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What happens to a society, or a heart, that fully pushes God out?
- Are you a protector of the vulnerable, standing against cruelty?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, this darkness sobers me. Keep my own heart from drifting toward using or harming others. Make me a person of justice and mercy, a protector of the vulnerable, shining as light in a dark world.
Amen.
